conclusion.title: CFP Executive Summary: Is LIC New Jeevan Anand Plan 715 Right For You?
conclusion.body: LIC New Jeevan Anand (Plan 715 / UIN: 512N279V03) remains LIC's premier double-cover combination policy. Unlike traditional pure endowment plans where life cover terminates at maturity, Jeevan Anand continues to provide full life cover (equal to the Basic Sum Assured) for the policyholder's entire life even after receiving the full maturity payout. It generates tax-free returns under Section 10(10D) of ~6.0% p.a. combined with premium deductions under Section 80C. For broader financial planning, explore our Jeevan Labh Calculator for limited pay options, Jeevan Umang Calculator for 8% pension, Surrender Value Calculator, Maturity Calculator, FD vs PPF Calculator, and Tax Regime Calculator.

sections.title: The Mathematics of Plan 715: Tabular Rates, Rebates & GST Logic

content.text:
How the Exact Premium is Computed Actuarially

Unlike basic online tools that use crude approximations, our calculator applies official LIC actuarial formulas, modal payment rebates, High Sum Assured (HSA) deductions, and split GST tiers:

Net Annual Premium = [(Sum Assured / 1000) × Base Tabular Rate - HSA Rebate - Modal Discount] × (1 + GST Tier)

content.footer: Modal Payment Discounts: Yearly Payment Mode receives a 2% tabular rate discount. Half-Yearly Mode receives a 1% tabular rate discount.

content.text:
Maturity Payout Components

  • Basic Sum Assured (SA): The guaranteed base benefit selected at entry.
  • Vested Simple Reversionary Bonuses: Declared annually by LIC per ₹1,000 Sum Assured and accrued throughout the policy term (~₹42 to ₹48 per ₹1,000 SA).
  • Final Additional Bonus (FAB): A one-time loyalty bonus paid at maturity for policies with terms of 15 years or longer (~₹20 to ₹250 per ₹1,000 SA).
  • Post-Maturity Whole Life Risk Cover: Upon policy maturity, the full lump sum is paid out, AND the Basic Sum Assured continues as a tax-free life cover payable to the nominee upon death at any age.

sections.title: IRDAI Master Circular 2024 Rules: Surrender Value & Policy Loans

content.text: Under the revised IRDAI Master Circular 2024 rules, life insurance policyholders receive enhanced liquidity protections:

items: 1-Year Surrender Eligibility: Under IRDAI 2024 guidelines, policies acquire a guaranteed surrender value after completing just 1 full policy year (down from 2 years previously).
Guaranteed Surrender Value (GSV): Calculated as a percentage of total premiums paid (excluding GST and rider charges) plus the surrender value of accrued vested bonuses.
Special Surrender Value (SSV): Reflects the actuarial present value of accumulated benefits. LIC pays whichever is higher between GSV and SSV.
Policy Loan Facility: Policyholders can borrow up to 90% of the Special Surrender Value for active policies (80% for paid-up policies) at competitive interest rates (~9.5% p.a. simple interest).

content.title: CFP Recommendation: Surrender vs. Paid-Up Status
content.text: If you cannot pay premiums beyond 1–2 years, converting your policy to Paid-Up status is almost always superior to surrendering. Paid-Up policies retain proportional Sum Assured and post-maturity cover without forfeiting capital to surrender penalties. Estimate your surrender options using our LIC Surrender Value Calculator.

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) — LIC New Jeevan Anand (Plan 715 / 915)

items.q: What is the difference between LIC Plan 715 and Plan 915?
items.a: Plan 715 was the original New Jeevan Anand policy released under older IRDAI regulations. Plan 915 is the updated version introduced to comply with updated mortality tables and GST rules. The fundamental double death benefit and maturity calculation structure remain identical.

items.q: What makes LIC Jeevan Anand (Plan 715) unique compared to other endowment plans?
items.a: Jeevan Anand is the only endowment plan that provides a Double Death Cover: you receive the full maturity benefit (Sum Assured + Vested Bonuses + FAB) at the end of the policy term, AND the Basic Sum Assured continues as a lifelong risk cover payable to your nominee upon death at any age after maturity.

items.q: How is the Jeevan Anand maturity benefit calculated?
items.a: Maturity Benefit = Basic Sum Assured + Accrued Vested Simple Reversionary Bonuses + Final Additional Bonus (FAB). For example, a ₹10 Lakh SA policy over 25 years receives ₹10L SA + ₹12L Bonus + ₹1.5L FAB = ₹23.50 Lakhs maturity.

items.q: What is the death benefit during the policy term?
items.a: If demise occurs during the policy term, the nominee receives the 'Sum Assured on Death' (higher of 125% of Basic Sum Assured or 7x Annualized Premium) PLUS all vested bonuses accrued up to the date of death.

items.q: Are premiums and maturity payouts tax-exempt?
items.a: Yes. Premiums paid qualify for tax deductions up to ₹1,50,000 under Section 80C. Maturity and death benefits are completely tax-free under Section 10(10D) of the Income Tax Act.

items.q: Can I take a loan against my Jeevan Anand policy?
items.a: Yes. Policy loans are available after completing 1 full policy year under IRDAI 2024 guidelines. You can borrow up to 90% of the Special Surrender Value at simple interest rates.

items.q: What is the grace period for premium payments in Plan 715?
items.a: A grace period of 30 days is allowed for Yearly, Half-Yearly, and Quarterly payment modes, and 15 days for Monthly NACH mode.
